correctness.rationale: For u with nonempty linear support, rank(M_u)=1+rank(B_a). Kernel(B_a) consists of h_G(S) unconstrained outside coordinates plus one parameter per support component in characteristic two or per bipartite support component in odd characteristic. The edge-basis independence shows rank(M_u^2) equals one exactly for nonempty induced-edge support in odd characteristic. Empty linear support contributes 1 zero and q^m-1 nonzero pure-quadratic rank-one elements. The product count gives the claimed polynomial; M_u^3=0 gives Jordan multiplicities (3^s,2^(r-2s),1^(1+n+m-2r+s)). Direct finite-field matrix enumeration and a second support count agree in 99 full and 128 formula configurations.

originality.rationale: The prior full-support unsigned-incidence-map calculation from Dao–Nair is explicitly not claimed. The assessed new object is the support-refined, all-radical-element, two-rank Jordan counting polynomial for any finite graph and finite field, including characteristic two and quadratic coefficients. Closely read sources cover WLP, generic linear forms, paths/cycles, and Jordan surveys rather than the whole joint distribution. Priority risk from older equivalent combinatorial presentations remains.

No independent historical-priority or mathematical review is asserted.

value.rationale: The natural finite-field census of multiplication Jordan types for all radical elements extends weak-Lefschetz generic-form questions to a complete distribution. It gives exact frequencies and all blocks in every characteristic; its support coefficient recovers the graph degree multiset, and two nonisomorphic graph face algebras with identical Hilbert function yield different rank statistics. This is mathematically motivated by Artinian ring invariants rather than arbitrary parameter slicing.
